name: East Asian Studies (BA)

rules.name: Language Proficiency Requirement
rules.desc: This requirement applies to students who do not declare a subplan. Demonstrate proficiency in Chinese, Japanese, or Korean language at the second-year level or above, to be met either by coursework or examination.
rules.notes:
Students who meet the language proficiency requirement through examination are expected to do at least two of the following:

• Take an additional 15 units of the language at a higher level.

• Enroll in literature courses taught in the language.

• Complete the first-year course sequence of another East Asian language.
No more than 30 units of language courses may be counted toward the major.

rules.name: Area Courses Requirement
rules.desc:
Complete three area courses total, one in each of the following categories:

• Humanities

• History

• Social Sciences
Courses used toward the area courses requirement should have a thematic focus on East Asia and/or a region of East Asia and may be listed at any number level.
The listed courses are examples and not exhaustive; if uncertain whether a course fits into a specific category, please consult with the DUS and/or SSO.

rules.name: GPA of 2.0 in major courses and their prerequisites
Four thematically coherent East Asia courses (one numbered 200 or above)
rules.desc:
Complete four courses with a thematic coherence on East Asia, at least one of which must be numbered at the 200-level or above.
Examples of possible themes include:

• East Asian religions and philosophies

• Culture and society of modern Japan

• Ethnic identities in East Asia

• Arts and literature in late imperial China

• Foreign policy in East Asia

• Social transformation of modern Korea

• China's political economy

rules.name: Remaining units of the 78-unit minimum (eligible subjects)
Remaining units from other related departments, approved by the DUS
Writing in the Major (WIM)
rules.desc: To meet this requirement, you must complete one of the following EALC courses before your senior year. The course you choose should align with your declared subplan and/or academic interests. For guidance on which course to select, please refer to the subplan information in the relevant section. Students who do not declare a subplan may select any of the three courses.
rules.notes: Only one course may be used to fulfill the WIM requirement, and other EALC WIM courses taken will be counted toward other course requirements.

rules.name: Capstone Experience
rules.desc:
Submit one of the following as agreed upon by the DUS, faculty advisor, and student, and present the research to EALC peers and faculty:

• Capstone Essay (~7,500 words)

• Equivalent Alternate Project (e.g., translation, media production, etc.)

• Honors Thesis (~15,000 words)
The topic should be built upon the student’s thematic interest.
A faculty advisor for the capstone essay must be finalized no later than the second week of autumn quarter of the senior year.
Majors must enroll in the Senior Colloquium (EALC 198) in winter quarter of the senior year and enroll in at least one Senior Research course (EALC 198C or EALC 199) with their faculty advisor during the senior year.
Senior Capstone and Honors Thesis Presentations will be held in spring quarter. Students must present as part of their final project.
rules.notes: Students are required to enroll in EALC 198 in the winter quarter of the senior year and enroll in at least one Senior Research course (EALC 198C and/or EALC 199) with their faculty advisor during the senior year.

rules.name: Capstone essay, alternate project or honors thesis, presented in spring
Honors Requirement

children.name: Senior thesis proposal approved by the DUS (junior year)
One advanced-level colloquium or seminar on China, Japan or Korea

rules.desc:
Majors with an overall grade point average (GPA) of 3.5 may apply for the honors program by submitting a senior thesis proposal to the Director of Undergraduate Studies (DUS) during the winter or spring quarter of the junior year. The proposal must include:

• A thesis outline

• A list of all relevant courses the student has taken and plans to take; one advanced-level colloquium or seminar dealing with China, Japan, or Korea is required

• A preliminary reading list including a work or works in Chinese, Japanese, or Korean

• The name of a faculty member who has agreed to act as the honors topic advisor
Students must discuss the honors project with the DUS and receive approval before conducting honors research. Without approval, students should plan to complete the capstone essay.
More information about the honors program can be found on the EALC website.

To bring the total number of units counted towards the major to 78, complete the following courses selected with approval by the SSO, DUS, and/or advisor.

gpa: Courses as well as their prerequisites must be completed with a grade point average (GPA) of 2.0 or better.
grading: All courses used in fulfillment of non-language requirements must be taken for letter grading and at least 3 units each.
policies:
The courses taken for the major must add up to at least 78 units, comprised of EALC 198 and at least 75 additional units, all taken for a letter grade. Courses must be at least three units and taken with a letter grade to be counted towards the degree. Majors are encouraged to distribute their coursework among at least three disciplines and two subregions in Asia. The subregions need not be traditionally defined.
All courses used in fulfillment of non-language requirements must be taught by a Stanford faculty member with a primary or courtesy/affiliated appointment in the Department of East Asian Languages and Cultures.
Eligible subject codes for courses used in fulfillment of requirements include: CHINA, CHINLANG, JAPAN, JAPANLNG, KOREA, KORLANG, EALC, EASTASN, ANTHRO, ARTHIST, ASNAMST, COMPLIT, DLCL, ETHICSOC, FEMGEN, FILMEDIA, GLOBAL, HUMSCI, HUMCORE, INTLPOL, INTNLREL, LINGUIST, MTL, PHIL, POLISCI, PUBLPOL, RELIGST, STS, SOC, TAPS, URBANST, OSPBEIJ, OSPHONGK, OSPKYOTO, OSPKYOCT, and/or other related departments.
The Director of Undergraduate Studies (DUS) may approve changes or substitutions to the fulfillment of requirements.
transferPolicy: External credit may be used in fulfillment of requirements with approval of the Director of Undergraduate Studies (DUS). External credit options include courses taught by the Bing Overseas Studies Program (BOSP), by other colleges or universities outside of Stanford, or internship or other educational experiences in East Asia.
reviewNotes: Without a subplan you show second-year proficiency in Chinese, Japanese or Korean; a subplan instead asks for third-year proficiency and adds its own courses. Everyone takes three area courses (humanities, history, social sciences), four thematically coherent East Asia courses with one numbered 200 or above (moved in by hand), a WIM course, and the Senior Colloquium (EALC 198) with a Senior Research course and a capstone essay, project or honors thesis. Courses outside the language requirement must be letter graded and at least 3 units. The major needs 78 units: other courses in the eligible subjects count toward them, at most 30 units of language courses count, and courses from other related departments are moved in by hand with the DUS's approval. You check by hand the 2.0 GPA, that each non-language course is taught by a faculty member with an EALC appointment, the subplans' approved content courses, and proficiency shown by exam; honors adds a 3.5 GPA, an approved proposal, an advanced seminar and the thesis. With the China, Japan or Korea subplan the WIM course must be CHINA 111, JAPAN 138 or KOREA 120 respectively; the East Asian Languages subplan's additional courses can come from any one of its four categories.
